For a report of methaemoglobinaemia as a re- sult of the ingestion of cocaine adulterated with benzocaine, see Abuse under Adverse Effects of Benzocaine, p.1854. BREAST FEEDING. The American Academy of Pediatrics1 has stated that, when used as a drug of abuse by breast-feeding mothers, cocaine has caused signs of intoxication in the in- fant, notably diarrhoea, vomiting, irritability, seizures, and tremulousness.
